scans.explanation: The Swin Transformer V2-B model predicted Melanoma and the Grad-CAM map highlights pronounced structural asymmetry (A score: 1.8), marked border irregularity (B score: 2.1), and multi-colored variegation (C score: 3.2). Additionally, high-intensity local activation of the Vision Transformer self-attention maps points heavily to an atypical pigment network near the upper margin.
scans.clinicalDetails: Atypical melanocytic lesion showing dynamic asymmetry and jagged borders. Grad-CAM shows localized activation over the lesion region. Recommend immediate excisional biopsy with 5mm margins.

scans.explanation: The Swin Transformer V2-B model shows high confidence (97.2%) for a completely benign melanocytic nevus. On-screen features demonstrate excellent radial symmetry, sharp well-defined borders, and uniform brown pigment network distribution.
scans.clinicalDetails: Symmetrical dermoscopic structure. No atypical pigment networks, regression structures, or blue-white veils identified. Regular benign nevus pattern. Grad-CAM activations are uniformly spread with low concentration peak.

doctorVerdict.notes: Typical benign compound nevus. Symmetrical. No follow-up or biopsy required unless patient reports rapid changes or itching. Advised annual skin self-checks using ABCDE criteria.

scans.explanation: The model detected a high likelihood of Basal Cell Carcinoma, characterized by local telangiectasias (fine blood vessel lines) and a pearly translucent border structure highlighted by the Grad-CAM map.
scans.clinicalDetails: Nodular basal cell carcinoma candidate. Prominent shiny nodule. Grad-CAM maps show strong localized focus around translucent micro-structures. Biopsy is highly recommended.

doctorVerdict.notes: Pearly borders with minor telangiectasia. I agree with the model's high risk indicator. I recommend a punch biopsy to confirm Basal Cell Carcinoma. I have requested Rohan to schedule an in-person clinical visit.
